facts.statement: The name Annulicorona means 'ring crown' and refers to a ring structure at the base of the crown on its dermal denticles.
facts.quote: Its name comes from the Latin Annulis meaning ring and Corona meaning crown, referring to the ring around the base of the crown of dermal denticles.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from isolated dermal denticles belonging to the single species Annulicorona pyramidalis.
facts.quote: It is known from the isolated dermal denticles of a single species, A. pyramidalis.

facts.statement: The dermal denticles of this species have a crown that is roughly pyramid-shaped.
facts.quote: The name refers to the roughly pyramid-shaped crown of the referred dermal denticles.

facts.statement: Fossils of Annulicorona have been found at two sites in the Xiaowa Formation in Guizhou, China.
facts.quote: It is known from two Xiaowa Formation sites in Guizhou, China.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the middle Carnian stage of the Triassic period.
facts.quote: They are middle Carnian in age.

facts.statement: The exact classification of Annulicorona is uncertain because the known fossil remains are very fragmentary.
facts.quote: Its affinities are uncertain due to the fragmentary nature of known remains.

facts.statement: Annulicorona belongs to the parent group Elasmobranchii.
Annulicorona is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The type species for the genus Annulicorona is Annulicorona pyramidalis.
Annulicorona lived between 237 and 233.6 million years ago during the Carnian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 233.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Annulicorona is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that lived during the Upper Triassic epoch.
rejected.quote: Annulicorona is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish from Upper Triassic epoch of the Triassic period.
